rules.statement: Before implementation, framework-context, or substantial documentation changes, ensure an Issue records why the change exists; it may be brief.
rules.title: Back every change with an Issue
rules.why: Repository history should show the reason without reconstructing chat history.

rules.statement: Before starting a new coherent development block, record a short purpose and checklist in the project's durable planning surface; use `PLAN.md` when the project follows this workflow convention.
rules.title: Plan a coherent change block before editing
rules.why: Repository state must explain what work is in progress even if the chat, model session, or tool run disappears.

rules.statement: When a listed step is actually complete, mark its `PLAN.md` checkbox `[x]` immediately rather than reconstructing completion at the end of a long session.
rules.title: Checkpoint completed plan items immediately
rules.why: Immediate checkpoints turn PLAN into a reliable recovery ledger instead of requiring plan archaeology after an interruption.

rules.statement: Put decisions, active constraints, accepted state, and next steps needed to resume work in repository documentation such as `PLAN.md`, `STATE.md`, or the project's equivalent rather than relying on chat history or model memory.
rules.title: Keep recovery-critical knowledge in the repository
rules.why: Long conversations and agent sessions are transient; the repository is the durable shared recovery point for humans and tools.

rules.statement: When the project owner resumes work after a short conversational interruption, explicitly says to continue, and reports no intervening repository changes, continue from the last established branch/PR state unless a repository operation gives evidence that it changed. Do not spend a new work cycle re-checking already established repository facts merely to prove that nothing happened.
rules.title: Resume recent explicit continuation without re-proving unchanged state
rules.why: In a controlled single-owner workflow, repeated defensive re-verification consumes the useful working window without adding evidence. Any stated or observed intervening change still invalidates this assumption.

rules.statement: When Markdown is also parsed, compiled, extracted, or otherwise given machine-significant meaning, every field or wording whose value affects machine semantics must live in an explicitly marked machine structure rather than being inferred from ordinary presentation prose. Keep that machine significance recognizable in rendered and review surfaces; rendering may style or summarize the control structure, but must not make the machine/human boundary indistinguishable.
rules.title: Mark machine-significant Markdown explicitly
rules.why: Humans must be able to tell which Markdown is freely editable presentation and which content participates in operational semantics; hidden parser contracts turn harmless-looking prose edits into surprising behavior.

rules.statement: When writing Markdown links to repository-local files or directories, keep the real filesystem path as the semantic source of truth but percent-encode the Markdown link destination as a URI path instead of embedding raw spaces or Markdown/URL-sensitive path characters.
rules.title: Render repository-local Markdown links URL-safely
rules.why: Valid repository filenames can contain spaces, `#`, `%`, parentheses and other characters that Markdown consumers parse differently; URL-safe link destinations keep links portable across IDEs, GitHub and other renderers without forcing artificial filename restrictions.

rules.statement: For tool-owned disposable directories, use a shared bounded-retry deletion method, tolerate empty leftovers from temporary filesystem locks, and retry later. Never follow links or remove unknown files; fail on missing or corrupt authoritative data. Follow the detailed method in `docs/filesystem-cleanup.md`.
rules.title: Treat directory cleanup as best-effort, but authoritative data as strict
rules.why: Windows antivirus/indexers and other concurrent processes can outlive a cleanup attempt. One transient lock must not break a later unrelated build, but cleanup tolerance must never hide lost project data.

rules.statement: For one coherent correction block, make the related authoring/code changes and run proportionate focused checks first; do not repeat the project's most expensive generated-output, integration, packaging, or full verification cycle after every micro-edit.
rules.title: Batch related edits before expensive final verification
rules.why: Final verification is valuable, but repeating it on superseded intermediate heads adds ceremony without increasing confidence in the candidate that will actually be reviewed or merged.

rules.statement: When the project owner explicitly approves a coherent implementation scope and says intermediate product review is unnecessary, mark the Fast Track as active in the durable PLAN with its scope and exit condition, keep recovery checkpoints and focused verification inside bounded work blocks, and defer repeated PR-description polish, full CI, generated-output regeneration, and other review ceremony until the coherent review candidate. When the Fast Track ends, record that closure before returning to ordinary review cadence.
rules.title: Use owner-approved Fast Track blocks without weakening the final gate
rules.why: Explicit delegation can remove intermediate coordination cost without sacrificing recoverability. Visible start/scope/exit/closure boundaries prevent a long single-worker Fast Track from becoming undocumented process state, while final human review and exact-head merge verification remain unchanged.

rules.statement: A coherent development block may be presented for project-owner review while understood and disclosed CI failures or generated drift remain. After explicit project-owner approval and before merging, require the exact current head to pass the project's complete merge-gate verification, including zero generated drift when generated canonical output is part of the project contract.
rules.title: Require exact-head green verification at the merge gate, not the first review gate
rules.why: Human review should happen before spending finalization effort on a candidate that may still change, while the accepted branch remains protected by a strict reproducibility gate.

rules.statement: When actively testing an installable Python tool from a development checkout, prefer one editable install (`uv tool install --editable .`) and pull subsequent revisions with Git rather than reinstalling each version, when the environment supports it.
rules.title: Prefer editable installs for repeated owner testing
rules.why: This keeps the owner-test loop short and makes the tested command follow the current checkout.

rules.statement: When an executable tool is tested from a changing Git checkout, keep its release version stable until a real release/version boundary, but make runtime version output identify the current VCS state with the branch/ref when available, commit identity, and dirty state. Treat the commit identity as authoritative and the branch/ref as human orientation; release artifacts without checkout metadata still report the canonical release version.
rules.title: Expose development provenance without micro-bumping releases
rules.why: Humans and agents must be able to distinguish different development code behind the same release baseline without turning every branch, documentation edit, or review iteration into release-version ceremony.

rules.statement: Applicable Context constrains a task; it does not silently expand its writable scope.
rules.title: Expand change scope explicitly
rules.why: A local task must not acquire wider impact merely because broader Context was loaded.

rules.statement: Keep a review PR or equivalent change set open until the project owner explicitly approves the reviewed result.
rules.title: Do not merge without explicit project-owner approval
rules.why: Green automation proves only the properties it checks; it does not prove that the product, architecture, or documentation is acceptable to its human owner.

rules.statement: After a reviewed change is successfully merged into the accepted branch, reconcile the durable repository state that records the accepted baseline before starting the next coherent development block. Record the merge outcome in `PLAN.md`, update `STATE.md` or equivalent current-state documentation, and refresh README/CHANGELOG or review-status wording made stale by the merge when applicable.
rules.title: Close the post-merge baseline checkpoint before new development
rules.why: The merge itself creates project facts after the merge candidate was frozen. Without a post-merge checkpoint, the accepted code can be correct while recovery documentation still describes the pre-merge state.

rules.statement: Manage workflow Issues, Pull Requests, reviews, checks/CI status, and merge state in the project's GitHub repository. Branches and commits remain ordinary Git objects; when a capable local harness is available, edit and test the local working tree directly rather than treating GitHub file APIs as a substitute filesystem.
rules.title: Use GitHub development objects
rules.why: The workflow should use standard GitHub semantics and tools while local code work stays local when possible.

rules.statement: Maintain each configuration fact once in the layer that owns it; do not put engine flags in profiles, model paths in engine files, or duplicate model sampling defaults. Shared instance configuration must not duplicate operating-system-specific runtime paths; launchers should supply machine-local binary and model roots explicitly, with environment variables only as documented optional fallbacks. Backend-specific process environment such as GPU-selection variables belongs in the engine configuration and is applied by Dispatcher when it launches llama.cpp rather than being required in the caller's shell. Instance repositories under `instances/<name>/` are user-owned independent Git repositories: Dispatcher core ignores their contents and must not register or manage them as Git submodules.
rules.title: Keep configuration in its owning layer
rules.why: Clear ownership prevents conflicting configuration, repeated maintenance, and hidden ambient startup state.

rules.statement: Configuration is deep-merged in this order: model defaults, instance engine defaults, profile, ensemble model entry; ad-hoc llama.cpp CLI overrides have highest priority.
rules.title: Configuration precedence
rules.why: A deterministic precedence order makes the effective llama.cpp configuration predictable.

rules.statement: Manage dependencies with uv rather than direct pip, conda, or poetry commands, and run tests or project executions through uv run.
rules.title: Use uv for project dependency and execution workflows
rules.why: The project uses one dependency and execution workflow to keep environments consistent.

rules.statement: Strictly separate observed, declared, and unknown facts.
rules.title: Separate observed, declared, and unknown facts
rules.why: Implementation and documentation should not turn assumptions into asserted project facts.

rules.statement: Configuration describes intent; code implements it, never the other way around.
rules.title: Configuration states intent
rules.why: Runtime transformation should follow explicit configuration instead of hidden code-side policy.

rules.statement: Prefer small, understandable changes.
rules.title: Prefer small understandable changes
rules.why: Small coherent changes are easier to review, test, and reason about.

rules.statement: Normalize parameter keys by removing leading dashes, replacing underscores with dashes, and mapping known shorthands or aliases to canonical long forms without leading dashes.
rules.title: Canonicalize parameter names
rules.why: One canonical representation prevents silent mismatches across defaults, profiles, ensembles, CLI input, and telemetry.

rules.statement: Add new llama.cpp parameters to PARAM_MAPPING in dispatcher.py when shorthand or spelling canonicalization is required.
rules.title: Register new llama.cpp parameters
rules.why: The mapping is the explicit source for translating accepted aliases into canonical parameter names.

rules.statement: For parameters configured by the selected alias, Dispatcher policy overwrites client values; request parameters not managed by that alias pass through unchanged.
rules.title: Dispatcher policy overrides managed client values
rules.why: Central configuration must be authoritative without blocking unrelated OpenAI-compatible or future llama.cpp request fields.

rules.statement: When chat_template_kwargs is configured for an alias, replace the client object with the configured object rather than recursively merging it.
rules.title: Replace chat_template_kwargs as one policy value
rules.why: The runtime treats chat_template_kwargs as one Dispatcher policy value.

rules.statement: Preserve client intent before transformation and log the request resolution and effective values after policy enforcement and optional target remapping.
rules.title: Preserve and log request transformation
rules.why: Telemetry must show both what the client requested and what llama.cpp actually received.

rules.statement: Exclude messages, prompt, and input from proxy parameter snapshots while retaining request control parameters.
rules.title: Do not duplicate prompt content in proxy telemetry
rules.why: Telemetry should capture request controls without duplicating conversation or prompt content.

rules.statement: In ensemble operation, clients must connect to the Dispatcher proxy rather than directly to the internal llama.cpp server.
rules.title: Clients must use the Dispatcher proxy
rules.why: Direct llama.cpp access bypasses virtual aliases, Dispatcher parameter injection, alias remapping, and proxy telemetry.

rules.statement: Do not modify an execution_runs record after it has been written.
rules.title: Execution runs are immutable historical headers
rules.why: execution_runs is the historical run header.

rules.statement: Record exactly one serve_model_instance even in Single Profile Mode.
rules.title: Record a runtime model instance in every mode
rules.why: Evaluations remain homogeneous between single-profile and ensemble modes.

rules.statement: Validate external FastAPI endpoint payloads with Pydantic models or explicit validation.
rules.title: Validate FastAPI payloads
rules.why: External request data must be checked before it enters orchestration logic.

rules.statement: Do not use blocking calls such as time.sleep or subprocess.run in the orchestrator; start subprocesses and consume their logs asynchronously.
rules.title: Keep orchestration non-blocking
rules.why: Blocking calls would stall the asynchronous service.

rules.statement: metrics_bench.speed_error is mandatory.
rules.title: Benchmark speed error is mandatory
rules.why: Benchmark measurements should carry their uncertainty.

rules.statement: metrics_eval.perplexity_error is mandatory where available.
rules.title: Perplexity error is mandatory when available
rules.why: Evaluation measurements should carry their uncertainty when it can be computed.

rules.statement: Do not record a measurement without an error value when repetitions are available.
rules.title: Repeated measurements require an error value
rules.why: Repeated measurements provide the information needed to report uncertainty.

rules.statement: Make new features testable first with --compile-only or /debug/preview where applicable.
rules.title: Make new behavior previewable before full operation
rules.why: Configuration and request transformations should be inspectable before a full runtime path is exercised.

rules.statement: For schema evolution, avoid destructive updates to existing measurement data, use PRAGMA user_version, and map migrations in a controlled manner in database_manager.py.
rules.title: Future schema evolution safeguards
rules.why: Measurement history must remain trustworthy across future schema changes.

rules.statement: Store parameter names in canonical dashed form in the database, but write OpenAI-compatible request JSON keys with underscores when forwarding to llama.cpp.
rules.title: Store canonical DB keys and OpenAI JSON keys
rules.why: Internal canonicalization and the external OpenAI-compatible API use different naming conventions.
